source_name: Ditec a.s. – produkty a služby (e-signature / eIDAS stack)
why_relevant: Ditec is the dominant SK supplier of qualified e-signature, bulk signing and guaranteed-conversion components that banks embed for paperless onboarding and archiving; product pages reveal the compliance building blocks competitors resell.

source_name: Aliter Technologies a.s. – corporate site
why_relevant: Fast-growing Slovak-Canadian ICT firm (2025 revenue ~EUR 71m per FinStat) active in secure communications and infrastructure; a credible bidder against integrators for bank infrastructure and security work.

source_name: LYNX Information Systems & Security Solutions – Referencie
why_relevant: Newly discovered (not in seed actor list) SK integrator whose reference page names Tatra banka and VÚB in the financial segment — expands the competitor set beyond the assumed actors.

source_name: EEA s.r.o. – Referencie filtered to 'Banky a finančný sektor'
why_relevant: Rare example of a SK software house exposing a segment-filtered reference query string, i.e. a machine-friendly list of its banking clients; also an actor missing from the seed list.

source_name: Gratex International a.s. – corporate site
why_relevant: Long-standing Bratislava software house historically strong in insurance/financial back-office and government; relevant as a bidder and as an employer-of-record for financial-domain engineering capacity in SK.

source_name: DATALAN a.s. – corporate site
why_relevant: One of the largest SK integrators (business solutions, IT outsourcing, consulting) and a habitual prime contractor; needed for completeness of the competitor set even though banking references were not confirmed in this pass.

source_name: FinReg.sk – Slovak financial register profiles
why_relevant: Alternative financial-profile aggregator useful when FinStat is rate-limited; carried the Gratex International profile when the vendor's own site was not surfaced.

source_name: uvostat.sk – analytics over Slovak public procurement (ÚVO) awards
why_relevant: Maps which SK IT firms bid together and win together ('kto s kým v štátnych IT súťažiach'). Although the tenders are public-sector, the consortium and subcontracting patterns are the same ones used for state-owned and partly-state banks, and reveal prime/sub relationships invisible on marketing sites.

source_name: OPIS dodávatelia – historic dataset of Slovak IT programme suppliers
why_relevant: Independent compilation of which firms (Soitron, Ditec, Gratex etc.) supplied the large SK informatisation programme; a durable archival map of the local prime-contractor landscape and its consortium habits.

source_name: Denník E / Denník N – business reporting on Slovak IT suppliers' revenues
why_relevant: Independent journalism that ranks SK IT suppliers by revenue and contract capture — an editorial cross-check against vendor self-reporting, and a source of names not present on any reference page.

source_name: Erste Digital (Slovenská sporiteľňa / Erste Group captive IT hub)
why_relevant: Erste Digital runs Bratislava and Košice engineering sites with 2,000+ IT staff — the clearest example of a bank-owned service hub that insources work otherwise bought from SK integrators. Its hiring and org signals indicate which capabilities banks are pulling in-house vs outsourcing.

source_name: Centire – Finančné inštitúcie: vybrané projekty a referencie
why_relevant: Consulting-side supplier with a page dedicated to financial-institution engagements; captures the advisory layer that often precedes and shapes SK bank technology procurement.

source_name: NBS – Zoznam účastníkov platobného systému SIPS
why_relevant: Participant list for the domestic SIPS clearing system — reveals which banks/PSPs have direct clearing access in SK versus those riding on a sponsor, a key structural fact about the payments landscape.

source_name: NBS – SEPA Instant Credit Transfer / payment instruments & payment cards statistics
why_relevant: Official SK card, terminal and instant-payment adoption data — the denominator for any POS/terminal estate or A2A market-share estimate; also the SCT Inst adoption page tracking which SK PSPs joined the scheme.

source_name: European Payments Council – Registers of Participants (SCT Inst, SCT, SDD, SRTP, SPAA, OCT Inst, VOP)
why_relevant: Scheme-level ground truth on which SK-country PSPs have adhered to each SEPA scheme and when — the cleanest way to track SK instant-payments/A2A readiness per institution; downloadable registers, refreshed regularly.

source_name: Global Payments Slovensko – corporate site, POS offers and pricing pages
why_relevant: Largest-profile acquirer in SK (operating as Global Payments s.r.o. since 2016, tied to the Slovenská sporiteľňa channel). Its dated campaign pages (ponuka-pos-2025 / ponuka-pos-2026) expose terminal line-ups, bundled gateway, and pricing/subsidy promotions — a direct read on competitor commercial posture.

source_name: Worldline Slovensko – merchant terminals & financial-institution acquiring/ATM pages
why_relevant: Worldline runs an SK-localised merchant business (Yomani, Yoximo, Valina, Axium terminal families) plus a financial-institution line covering acquiring processing and ATM management — the clearest public view of which terminal hardware and outsourced processing sit in the SK estate. A separate SK micro-site platobnyterminal.sk.worldline.com also exists.

source_name: Besteron (Seyfor group) – SK payment gateway & POS terminals
why_relevant: Slovak-origin PSP (founded 2014, part of Czech Seyfor group since 2021) holding an NBS payment-institution licence, offering both gateway and POS terminals — a domestic competitor whose product/pricing pages and merchant references track SK SME acceptance.

source_name: TrustPay – SK-licensed pan-EEA payment institution
why_relevant: Founded in Slovakia in 2009, passporting across the EEA on an NBS payment-institution licence; strong in SK/CZ online-banking buttons. Key domestic PSP competitor; site carries product, pricing and merchant-segment material. URL inferred from repeated references — treat as unverified until the liveness pass runs.

source_name: ComGate – gateway comparison blog and SK/CZ product pages
why_relevant: CZ-origin PSP active in SK; publishes its own competitor comparison of SK/CZ gateways (self-serving but a useful actor map and method/currency matrix) alongside product and pricing pages.

source_name: 24-pay s.r.o. (Žilina) – gateway + POS terminals, NBS licence ODB-8835-5/2012
why_relevant: Long-standing domestic SK payment institution offering both gateway and POS terminals; explicitly publishes its NBS licence number. Useful for the mid-tier domestic competitor layer often missing from international market maps.

source_name: SKPAY, a.s. – e-money institution (Viamo/QR bill payment rails)
why_relevant: Licensed SK electronic-money institution (authorised 4 July 2018, NBS-supervised) behind consumer A2A/QR bill-payment services incl. PAY by square invoice payment at post offices — a distinctly non-bank A2A actor in the SK ecosystem. Its NBS subject page gives the authoritative licence record.

source_name: Webhostingcentrum.sk – comparison of 15+ payment gateways for SK/CZ e-shops
why_relevant: Maintained, dated (2026) independent comparison naming a long tail of gateways serving SK e-shops — an efficient way to snowball the full actor list (including small domestic players) and to see published fee levels side by side.

source_name: Podnikajte.sk – Porovnanie platobných brán na Slovensku
why_relevant: Mainstream SK SME business portal comparing gateways including bank-owned ones (CardPay by Tatra banka, eCard by VÚB) — captures the bank-acquiring arm layer that pure-fintech comparisons miss.

source_name: Bezhotovostne.sk – SK cashless-payments news, PAY by square bank support tracker
why_relevant: Niche SK outlet tracking which banks/apps support PAY by square and other acceptance topics; useful for feature-adoption tracking per institution rather than corporate PR.

source_name: TOUCHIT / BrandIT press-release service – card-scheme SK press releases (Mastercard, Visa)
why_relevant: Carries scheme PR verbatim for the SK market — e.g. Mastercard's August 2026 release on mobile payment penetration (56%) and tokenisation share. Effective proxy for scheme-level SK activity and for the survey data schemes release locally.

source_name: SAEC – Slovenská asociácia pre elektronický obchod (+ bezpecnynakup.sk certification)
why_relevant: SK e-commerce association; co-publishes market studies with MNFORCE on how Slovaks pay online (payment-method mix, incl. the reported rebound of cash-on-delivery from 18% to 25%), and runs the bezpecnynakup.sk e-shop certification list — a directory of merchants and, indirectly, their payment stacks.

source_name: Ecommerce Bridge SK – SK e-commerce trade media (payment-method studies)
why_relevant: Trade outlet publishing the SAEC/MNFORCE e-commerce studies and gateway/merchant news; a practical early-warning channel for PSP partnership and platform-integration announcements in SK e-commerce.
